Rulehouse

Download Now

Master a new form of chess across the globe! Fifteen different levels, all with different rules, locations, and funny characters!


Play the original version here!

Controls 

  • Left Click - Move Pieces, Interact with Buttons
  • Right Click - Return Pieces, Cancel Premove
  • R Key - Refresh Level
  • Mouse Wheel Click - Refresh Level

bigfy4 hours ago(+2)

The cutscenes and art style are top-notch—absolute stunners for this aesthetic! The backstory is super concise, logical, and funny too. Plus, the menus and navigation are crystal clear.

The core game mechanic is extremely creative and a lot of fun. At first, I thought, 'Oh great, do I have to learn a whole new set of chess rules from scratch?' But it started out with just pawns, which made the onboarding super smooth. I managed to pick up all the mechanics naturally as they were introduced, one by one.

My first real challenge was the Spain level with the cow/horse piece. Honestly, it would've been easier to just say it moves like a chess knight, because the art made it look a bit more complex than it actually was. That level was a bit of a hurdle, but I really enjoyed overcoming it.

However, right after that, I hit the monkey level, and it just completely killed my enthusiasm. I ended up closing the game and didn't feel any desire to go back and tackle that challenge.

Overall, huge congrats on the game, though!

P.S. Quick tactical thought on the 4v4 pawn race mechanic: since it's a symmetrical, perfect-information abstract game on a tight board, does Player 1 always have a built-in mathematical advantage? Felt like going first dictates the whole tempo.

Dalichrome1 day ago (1 edit) (+2)

Hiding behind another piece, means you can't get shot. Between shots, you get a free move because of the gun jamming. So the intent is to slowly move up with cover. We had some feedback that it was more fun to figure out than explain, but we're definitely open to tutorial-izing more. Hope it wasn't frustrating and you enjoyed otherwise!
